Antiepileptics are among the drugs used to manage neuropathic pain, which is often insensitive to opioid analgesics (see Choice of Analgesic, p.2). Carbamazepine ap- pears to be the antiepileptic most frequently used, but oxcar- bazepine has also been tried in various neuropathic pain syndromes1 including painful diabetic neuropathy2-4 (see p.6), postherpetic neuralgia5,6 (p.9), complex regional pain syndrome7 (p.6), glossopharyngeal neuralgia,8 oxaliplatin-induced neuropathy9 (see p.758), and trigeminal neuralgia (p.9). 1.
